subject: Boreal Payroll — v5.0 quant profile deployment causing latency & errors
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@borealpayroll.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike after model upgrade (v5.0, Q4)

Jonas / Marissa —

We pushed the new endpoint last night that you recommended (model v5.0 with Q4 quant profile). Since about 02:30 UTC this morning we see a ~3-4x p99 increase, p95 up by ~2x and a visible rise in 5xx error rate across our account (attached sample traces + p95/p99 CSV). This is impacting payroll run throughput and causing timeouts in our nightly batch job.

Key asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood rolled any runtime/quant changes for our Dedicated pool?
- We need an immediate rollback or a mitigation plan — this is blocking payroll processing.

I can be available on a quick bridge. Ccing Asha (SRE) who has the traces.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
CTO, Boreal Payroll
Attachment: performance_report_p95_p99.csv

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@borealpayroll.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after model upgrade (v5.0, Q4)

Sanjay —

Thanks for the heads-up and the traces. We see the same signal on our side correlating with the v5.0 rollout and the new Q4 quant profile. I'm escalating internally now.

Immediate steps from Redwood:
1) Open ticket INF-4321 (link below) and assign on-call infra.
2) Collect KV-cache and request sampling for your tenant.
3) Prepare rollback to v4.x + previous quant profile on a canary subset to validate.

We're standing up a 30-minute bridge — KarThik (ops) and Irene (model team) are joining. Will update within 15 minutes.

— Jonas
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production latency spike after model upgrade (v5.0, Q4)

Team —

Quick notes from the initial telemetry (INF-4321):
- Host-level metrics show steady GPU utilization but per-request latency increased, pointing at decoding/quant-path stalls rather than GPU saturation.
- Error traces include repeated DecodeTimeout + kernel fallback logs for specific sequence lengths around 512-768 tokens.
- We saw a fallback to slower kernels when KV cache hit rates were low (tied to batch shape variance).

Proposed immediate mitigation:
- Revert Boreal's lane to the previous quant profile (Q2 equivalent) for their Dedicated pool. This should restore the old kernel path.
- If revert is risky during payroll window, we can pin traffic to v4.x for night jobs only.

I'll start the rollback runbook unless model team flags a dependency.

— Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Attachment: trace_sample_20270610.txt

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike after model upgrade (v5.0, Q4)

Agree with Karthik's assessment. Additional model-team observations:
- v5.0 introduced a new attention kernel that benefits longer sequences but regresses for the 512-768 band when combined with aggressive Q4 packing.
- We have a quick toggle to disable the adaptive kernel selection and force the stable kernel path — lower risk than full model rollback.

Plan:
T-minus 10 minutes: apply kernel-toggle for Boreal's Dedicated pool and monitor p95/p99. If no improvement in 10m, execute rollback to v4.x and Q2 profile for their reserved pool.

I'll coordinate the canary and push the toggle.

— Irene
Model Ops Lead

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@borealpayroll.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Asha Menon <asha.m@borealpayroll.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after model upgrade (v5.0, Q4)

Jonas / team —

Thank you for the fast response. We're in the middle of nightly payroll runs; any improvement is welcome. Please keep us posted on the bridge. Also: our CFO has asked for an estimate of potential downtime / credits if this requires rollback. Our legal team may request an exec-level call if the window stretches beyond 2 hours.

Attaching a screenshot of the monitoring dashboard we shared with ops.

— Sanjay

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@borealpayroll.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after model upgrade (v5.0, Q4)

Sanjay —

Quick post-mitigation summary and next steps: the model-team applied the kernel-toggle on your Dedicated pool at 10:12 UTC on 2027-06-10. You should have observed a p99 reduction within the first 8–12 minutes. We continued to monitor overnight and saw stabilization of p95/p99 to within 10% of pre-upgrade baselines; 5xx errors dropped to normal.

Actions taken:
- Applied kernel-toggle (non-invasive) to force stable decode kernel for boreal tenant.
- Kept v5.0 model variant in place while avoiding the adaptive kernel path.
- Opened INF-4321 for postmortem; we will run a quantization profile audit and add a test in the pre-release harness for 512–768 token shapes.

Commercial note: given the disruption during a critical payroll window, we will apply a one-time invoice credit for the affected night and offer a technical review with your eng leadership to prevent recurrence. Vivek (VP Sales) is looped for the commercial follow-up.

If you want a full rollback to v4.x instead of staying on v5.0+toggle, we can schedule a safe window; it is not required for immediate stability.

Thanks for your partnership — we will follow up with a detailed RCA by EOD Monday and the remediation timeline for the quant profile test coverage.

— Jonas
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
